card: Adds a TxCollection mining IPC interface that allows external services, such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers (JDS), to assemble and validate candidate block templates from a list of WTXIDs without maintaining duplicate mempool mirrors. External template coordinators currently face high bandwidth and memory overhead synchronizing mempool data or serializing full blocks across IPC. The interface resolves WTXIDs against the local mempool, accepts missing transaction payloads, and validates the assembled block against the active chain tip using TestBlockValidity. This work enables downstream custom job validation in Stratum v2, demonstrated in sv2-apps PR #599.
changed_since_previous: No structural changes to commits or design approach; the PR has been rebased and refined.
evidence: Downstream implementation and end-to-end integration is demonstrated in Stratum v2 Reference Implementation pull request stratum-mining/sv2-apps#599.
Aligns with the Stratum v2 Job Declaration Protocol specification and Template Provider draft specification (sv2-spec discussion #239).
problem: External mining services that validate and approve miner-selected templates, such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers (JDS), need to verify proposed blocks against the chain tip without transmitting all transactions across the IPC boundary. Without in-node reconstruction, external services either must maintain their own redundant mempool mirrors or transfer full transaction sets over IPC, wasting memory and bandwidth.

risk.why: A flaw in template assembly or validation could cause miners to reject valid candidate templates or erroneously approve invalid blocks prior to mining.

scope_notes: Touches Cap'n Proto IPC definitions (mining.capnp), interfaces, node mining utilities, unit tests, and functional test harness code for IPC.
summary: Adds a TxCollection interface to the mining subsystem and Cap'n Proto IPC to allow external callers to reconstruct and validate block templates from an ordered list of witness transaction IDs (WTXIDs). The interface matches WTXIDs against the node's local mempool, reports missing transaction indices, ingests missing transaction payloads, and builds a candidate block template. It also refactors coinbase generation out of BlockAssembler::CreateNewBlock into a reusable helper so candidate blocks can be validated with either a node-generated dummy coinbase or a caller-supplied coinbase.
